newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe government to sell stake in steel firm.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe government to sell stake in steel firm.

text.p: The Zimbabwean government has decided to sell a majority of its shareholding in the country's ailing steelworks, Zisco, under a part-privatisation plan aimed at reviving the firm, a private consultant said on Wednesday.

Sanjeev Chhugani of Coopers and Lybrand said the government was looking for an investor to inject new life into Zisco, one of Africa's largest integrated steelworks, which has been plagued for years by management, production and cash problems.
Coopers and Lybrand are the consultants for the part- privatisation programme.
"The government has said it would like to get a strategic investor in Zisco and for that they expect to sell a majority shareholding in Zisco," Chhugani told Reuters.
However, he said the government, which has a stake of abut 90 percent in Zisco, had yet to decide how much of its shareholding it was willing to give up.
"There's no clear mandate as to how much they (the government) want to raise and how much shareholding they want to give up."
Government and Zisco officials were unavailable for comment.
Chhugani said the bid documents would be released next Tuesday and submissions would close on April 16 with successful bids being confirmed on May 14.

"The part privatisation of Zisco will introduce a technically competent investing partner that will lead to an improvement in Zisco's operational efficiency, access to markets and access to capital required to refurbish its production assets and meet working capital requirements," Coopers said in a statement.

The loss-making group has stayed afloat over the last decade on huge state subsidies. It has been operating at 30 percent capacity over the past four years because of delays in refurbishing its biggest blast furnace.

Last year, Zisco chairman Cornelius Sanyanga said a Chinese team had been contracted to start repairing the furnace under a Z$500 million (U.S.$46.2 million) agreement between China and Zimbabwe signed in May.

"While Zisco has been a loss-maker for a number of years purely due to non-synchronised investment, plans are currently underway to turn the company around," acting Zisco chief executive Gabriel Masanga said in a statement released by Coopers.
"With planned refurbishments and streamlining of operations, Zisco has the potential to become a viable producer and a strategic investor will strengthen Zisco's position," he said.

Harare has been under pressure from Western donors to speed up privatisation of loss-making state firms seen draining the economy but President Robert Mugabe has repeatedly said his government would not be hurried as it wanted to ensure that the majority blacks would benefit from the programme.
